req_desc:
Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from `/app/run.json` on port 4173 (or `APP_PUBLIC_PORT`) and answers the health check, as set out in Deployment.

Sign-in and roles
Seeded people sign in with email and password, get a session cookie, and each role reaches only the screens and endpoints listed for it in API.

Member sees only their own work
A member sees only their own pieces, photos and balance, and any other piece answers 404, as stated in Business rules.

One error shape and order
Every error uses the single error body and the single precedence order stated in API.

Server boundary
The server enforces the same-origin, size and content-type limits in Server boundary, never serves source files or credentials, and starts while Kill Bill, MinIO or Mailpit is unreachable.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment variables in Configuration and secrets and never appears in source or in anything sent to the browser.

Ticket-booklet look
Every screen uses the bisque ground with no pure white, dark umber ink, hairline rules between panes and the type pairing described in Visual design.

Exact numerals with units
Every measurement, percentage and price on screen is set in the monospaced figures with its unit, as described in Visual design.

Status as words and cone glyph
Every piece and firing status appears as its status label with a cone glyph, never as colour alone.

Reachable controls and contrast
Every interactive control except the true-scale placed footprints is at least 44 by 44 px, and every text and control meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on all three viewports.

Seeded studio
A fresh start contains exactly the people, kilns, profiles, clay bodies and rate set listed in Seed data, with no pieces.

Live fee estimate
On the intake form the rounded sides, cubic inches and fee update in place within one second of each keystroke or unit switch, with no submit, and are announced in the Fee estimate region.

Firing fee arithmetic
The quote and the accepted fee follow the conversion, half-inch round-up, plate floor, discount, single rounding and minimum rules in Business rules, to the cent.

Member logs a piece
A signed-in member fills the intake form, attaches a photo, sees the fee, presses Accept and charge, and sees the new piece in My pieces with its frozen fee.

Photo attached only once stored
A photo counts as attached, and the form says so, only after the server confirms the object exists in storage, and the stored object is byte-for-byte the upload with its original content type.

Intake receipt email
Every accepted intake sends one receipt to the piece owner with the fee breakdown described in Services.

Intake replay safety
Repeating an intake with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original response without a second piece, charge or email, and a changed body under that key is refused with 409.

Phone intake
At 375 by 812 with touch the intake form is a single column with the camera-capable photo picker and the fee panel pinned in view, and every step works by tapping.

Intake field errors
Invalid intake input returns 422 with per-field messages, and the form shows them beside each field and in a linked error summary.

All-or-nothing intake
An intake whose photo, charge or receipt step fails creates no piece, leaves no unvoided charge, and answers 503 naming the failed step, as qualified in Business rules.

Intake outage messages
Each failed intake step shows and announces its own exact message from Feedback states.

Dated rate sets
The owner adds rate sets with an effective studio date, and a quote or intake uses the newest rate set already in effect on the studio date of acceptance.

Frozen piece fees
A piece's rounded sides, cubic inches and fee never change after acceptance, even when a newer rate set takes effect.

Owner changes rates
The owner opens Rates, saves a new rate set effective today, and a member's next fee estimate reflects it while earlier pieces keep their fees.

Footprint geometry rules
A placement is refused when its footprint crosses the shelf edge, covers a post or overlaps another footprint on that layer, with the reason and copy in Business rules.

Stage, clay, cone and height rules
A placement is refused when the piece needs a different stage, its clay is not rated for the firing's cone, its glaze cone differs, or the layer would exceed the post height, with the reason and copy in Business rules.

Kiln tech packs a shelf
The kiln tech picks a ticket, moves its true-scale footprint over the shelf, sees each refusal on the footprint, places it, and watches the stub leave the ticket column and the fill rise.

Placement announcements
Every placement, move, removal and refusal is announced in the Shelf announcements region with the exact copy from Feedback states.

Placements persist with history
Saved layer, coordinates and rotation come back unchanged after a reload, and every placement action is recorded in the piece history with who did it.

One winner for one spot
Of simultaneous placements that would overlap, or of the same piece, exactly one succeeds and the rest get 409.

Load fill and layer height
The load fill percentage and each layer's height label equal recomputation from stored placements by the formulas in Business rules.

Removing and moving placed pieces
While the firing is still building, a placed piece can be moved, rotated or removed, and a removed piece returns to the queue.

Keyboard-only packing
Picking, moving, rotating, placing, cancelling and removing footprints all work from the keyboard alone with the keys in Interactions, whichever board control has focus.

Load board at each breakpoint
The load board shows rail, shelf and tickets side by side at 1280 by 800, stacked panes at 768 by 1024 and a one-layer shelf carousel at 375 by 812, with no horizontal scrolling.

Board refresh keeps work in progress
The five-second board refresh brings in new tickets and firing status without closing an open placement panel, moving focus, clearing a half-typed rotation or overwriting a shown message.

Footprint and fill motion
Footprints lift, step and settle and the fill numeral counts to its new value within the durations in Motion and effects.

Reduced-motion stepper
With reduced motion requested, footprints jump between grid steps, the fill shows its final value at once and layers switch without sliding, with identical function and announcements.

True-scale shelf drawing
The centre pane draws the current layer to scale from above with its posts, half-inch grid and placed footprints labelled by piece number.

Firing lifecycle
Firings move building, firing, cooling, unloadable, unloaded only along the edges in Business rules, and every other transition is refused with its 409.

Schedule from the kiln profile
The server derives each firing's end and unload time from the profile snapshot taken at start and the hour length setting, as qualified in Business rules.

Server decides when to unload
The board shows Kiln still cooling and keeps Unload disabled until the server reports the firing unloadable, regardless of the browser clock, and enables it within six seconds after.

Firing a load
The kiln tech creates a firing, packs it, starts it, sees the cooling state, and once unloadable unloads it to a pickup shelf.

Ready on pickup shelf notice
Unloading a piece's last firing marks it ready and sends its owner the ready notice with the exact heading in Services.

Pickup reminder and lapse
A ready piece still uncollected sends one reminder at 14 studio days and becomes Uncollected at 21, as qualified in Business rules.

Pickup and collection
Staff see ready pieces with their pickup shelf and days waiting, mark one collected, and its owner then sees it as Collected.

Guest drop-off intake
Staff log a guest piece with name, email, photo and dimensions, which posts the guest charge, sends the guest receipt with a tracking link and leaves the piece awaiting payment.

Paid only when billing confirms
A drop-off shows Paid and joins the firing queue only after Kill Bill records a successful PURCHASE for its full amount, and a billing failure leaves it Owed.

Counter drop-off
At the counter screen staff log a guest piece, see the guest fee, take payment and see Paid with the piece in the queue.

Tracking link shows one piece
A tracking link shows exactly one piece's number, status and pickup shelf and nothing about any person or other piece.

Revoke and replace tracking links
The owner can revoke a tracking link or issue a new one that kills the old, and a dead link shows the no-longer-active copy.

Read-only tracking
A tracking link changes nothing: every request other than reading it is refused.

Guest follows a piece
A guest opens the emailed link on a phone and sees the status move from waiting through cooling to ready with the pickup shelf.

Damage reports at unload
During unload the kiln tech can report a glaze run or crack on any piece with an unload photo, creating an open damage report.

Evidence served as uploaded
Intake and unload photos come back from the app byte-for-byte with their original content type.

Damage settlement
The owner either confirms a damage report with a shelf charge, posted to the piece owner's Kill Bill account, or waives it, and settled reports cannot change.

Owner settles a glaze run
The owner opens a damage report, compares the intake and unload photos side by side, and posts or waives the shelf charge.

Studio figures recomputed
Amounts owed, pieces awaiting pickup and load fill on the Studio screen equal recomputation from Kill Bill and stored records at every load.

Counter payment for members
The owner records a member's counter payment as a Kill Bill PURCHASE for the full balance, and the owed amount drops only after Kill Bill confirms.

Billing outage banner
When Kill Bill is unreachable the Studio screen hides amounts owed and shows the exact billing outage banner, while fill and pickup figures still show.

Owner's weekly review
The owner opens Studio, sees what each account owes, how full each kiln is and how many pieces wait for pickup, and records a member's payment.
`/app/run.json` exists with exactly the string keys `_schema` (value `run-manifest-v1`), `install`, `build` and `serve`, and the app is started only through it.

`/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists every shipped package by name, version and licence, where shipped packages means the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`, plus the bundled font families.
Every shipped package and bundled font is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or, for fonts only, OFL-1.1.
The app stores state only in Postgres and MinIO: no SQLite, Redis, local JSON files or other datastore.
The provided service configuration and seeded credentials for Postgres, MinIO, Kill Bill and Mailpit are left untouched.
The browser loads no script, style, font or image from any origin other than the app's own, except photos served by the app itself.
All application source is TypeScript and `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with no errors.
